title: AI literacy at work
examples: When should I ask my supervisor about using AI tools for reports?
What is the difference between keeping information private and keeping it confidential?
Can you give an example of when disclosing information is legally required?

explain.say: Today we are learning about using AI responsibly at work.

draw.text: AI Use: Verify, Keep Private, Share When Needed

explain.say: First we must learn about verification of AI outputs.
For example, if AI suggests a historical date, you must check it.
Next we need to understand data confidentiality rules.

draw.center: What not to input into public AI

explain.say: For instance, never paste client names into a public AI tool.
Finally we must know when and how to disclose information.

faq.q: If AI gives me a statistic, how do I know if it is true?
faq.a: You must cross-reference the main statistics with the original, trusted source material. Always check the source material yourself before using the number.
asks: How do I fact-check AI output?

faq.q: What exactly does 'confidential' mean in a work setting?
faq.a: Confidential means information that is private and should only be seen by specific people. This often includes unreleased financial data or client personal details.
asks: Can I share client data with AI?

faq.q: When am I required to disclose information?
faq.a: You are required to disclose information when a contract or law specifically demands it. Always check your company's guidelines first.
asks: Is there a time to tell people things?

faq.q: Can I use AI for general brainstorming without worrying?
faq.a: You can use it for general ideas, but if the ideas relate to specific projects or clients, you must verify and protect the data.
asks: What is the risk level for general use?

faq.q: If I forget what is confidential, what should I do?
faq.a: If you are unsure if data is confidential, you must assume it is and ask your direct manager for clarification. It is always better to ask than to risk a breach.
asks: Who do I ask about data rules?
What if I am unsure about data sensitivity?

facts: Always treat AI-generated facts as drafts needing human review.
Never input proprietary or personally identifiable information into public AI models.
Confidentiality agreements legally restrict who can see certain data.
Disclosure obligations are usually defined by law or contract.

quiz.say: AI suggests a market growth rate of 12 percent for next quarter. What is the best immediate action?
quiz.show: AI suggests 12% growth rate. What next?

options.show: Use the 12 percent rate immediately in the presentation.
options.say: Use the 12 percent rate immediately in the presentation.

options.show: Delete the entire section and start over.
options.say: Delete the entire section and start over.

options.show: Ask a colleague to just confirm the number.
options.say: Ask a colleague to just confirm the number.

options.show: Cross-reference the main statistics with the original report.
options.say: Cross-reference the main statistics with the original report.

quiz.why: You must verify any specific data point, like a percentage, against the original source document to ensure accuracy.

wrong.0: This assumes the AI is perfectly correct, which is a common mistake.
wrong.1: This is an overreaction; the mistake is not knowing where to check the number.
wrong.2: While helpful, relying on one person is not the same as checking the primary source.

quiz.say: You are writing a summary of a client meeting. Which statement best protects client information?
quiz.show: Summarizing client meeting notes. Which is safest?

options.show: Use only general terms and remove all names.
options.say: Use only general terms and remove all names.

options.show: Keep the summary confidential and send it only to the boss.
options.say: Keep the summary confidential and send it only to the boss.

options.show: Cross-reference the main statistics with the original report.
options.say: Cross-reference the main statistics with the original report.

options.show: Disclose the summary to the whole team for review.
options.say: Disclose the summary to the whole team for review.

quiz.why: Removing specific identifiers like names maintains confidentiality while still allowing you to convey the core message.

wrong.1: Confidentiality is a status, not an action; you must actively remove identifying details.
wrong.2: This addresses verification, not the removal of private names from the summary.
wrong.3: This violates confidentiality by sharing restricted information too widely.

quiz.say: Your contract requires you to report sales figures to a regulatory body. This situation requires:
quiz.show: Contract requires reporting sales figures. What is needed?

options.show: Verify the figures using AI tools only.
options.say: Verify the figures using AI tools only.

options.show: Use only general terms and remove all names.
options.say: Use only general terms and remove all names.

options.show: Keep the data confidential and do not mention it.
options.say: Keep the data confidential and do not mention it.

quiz.why: When a contract or law mandates sharing information, that is a clear disclosure requirement.

wrong.0: Verification is needed, but it does not override a legal requirement to share the data.
wrong.1: If the law requires the specific figures, removing them would be incomplete.
wrong.3: Ignoring a contractual requirement is a breach of professional duty.
